purpose: What Word shows, as list strings and as REF \w / \n results, for list paragraphs whose ancestor levels no paragraph has numbered since they last restarted, for levels whose level text names a deeper level, and for the combinations of the two (#1254, #1262, #1263).
procedure: Minimal packages (content types, package and document rels, document.xml, numbering.xml, styles.xml) were opened in Word. Each numbered paragraph is bookmarked b1..bN, and a final unnumbered paragraph holds complex REF fields `REF bN \w \h` and `REF bN \n \h` for every bookmark. Through AppleScript, `update field` ran on every field, each field's code and result range were read back, and each paragraph's `list string of list format` was read. Paragraph text names the w:num and w:ilvl it uses: "p3 stdO1L2" is the third paragraph, numId of the stdO1 instance, ilvl 2 (see numIds). LibreOffice was not measured.
finding: An ancestor level that no paragraph has numbered since it last restarted (or ever) is shown at a start value: the value the restart recorded for it (the restarting paragraph's instance start), else the abstract w:start. An instance w:startOverride is not shown that way (override_l0_skipped "1(a)", legal_override_orphan "Section 1.01(a)").

Such a level stays at that shown value until a paragraph of its own numbers it (u_double_fill "1(a)(i)" "1(a)(ii)"; override_l0_skipped "1(a)" "1(b)"). That paragraph continues from the start of the instance whose paragraph first showed the level (x_fill_by_override_then_plain "1(f)"; z_fill_after_override_restart "2(b)" though "(e)" was shown), unless it is its instance's first paragraph on an overridden level, which applies the override (override_l1_skipped "1(e)").
Unnamed ancestors are shown too: a level the paragraph's level text does not name still counts as numbered from its start (unnamed_ancestors "(i)" then "(b)").

A level whose own level text names a deeper level is silent: its list string is empty, its counter still advances (silent_top_unused_beneath ".2"/".1"; deep_own_level "2."), a placeholder naming it from a deeper level renders as empty text (silent_ref_mid "1..i", silent_ref_top "[-1]"), and REF fields to it show 0.
REF \n gives the paragraph's own level text less one trailing period, with ancestors at their shown values (r2 "1(a)(i)").

REF \w walks up from the lowest level the own text names, as in issue-1236. On the way up it passes over a silent level and continues with the level directly above it (deep_own_level "1(i)", silent_mid "1(a)", issue-1236 deep2 "(a)"); and it passes over a level shown at a start value when some level above it has a paragraph (unnamed_ancestors "1(i)", legal_orphan_clause "ARTICLE II(a)", legal_l3_after_section "Section 1.01(i)"). A silent level with a paragraph counts as such a level (silent_top_used_then_deep "(a)", silent_ref_top_fresh_mid "(a)" and "[-2](a)"). When no level above has one, the shown level is kept (legal_orphan_clause "Section 1.01(a)", legal_l3_first "Section 1.01(a)(i)", unnamed_first_deep "1(a)(i)").
